response.sql: WITH per_media AS (SELECT MediaTypeId, AVG(UnitPrice) AS avg_price, 1.0 * SUM(Bytes) / SUM(Milliseconds) AS byte_rate FROM Track GROUP BY MediaTypeId), overall AS (SELECT AVG(byte_rate) AS avg_rate FROM per_media), above AS (SELECT p.avg_price, p.byte_rate, p.byte_rate - o.avg_rate AS excess FROM per_media p CROSS JOIN overall o WHERE p.byte_rate > o.avg_rate) SELECT AVG(avg_price) AS avg_of_avg_unit_price, AVG(byte_rate) AS avg_byte_rate, AVG(excess) AS avg_excess_over_overall FROM above;

assumptions.assumption: A track with NULL Bytes adds 0 to its media type's byte total, but its Milliseconds still count toward the denominator, since the request says 'total Bytes divided by total Milliseconds' over all its tracks.
The average unit price per media type is a plain AVG over all of its tracks, unweighted by quantity or sales.

Every media type has nonzero total Milliseconds, so no division by zero occurs. The 1.0 multiplier keeps the byte rate fractional, so nothing is truncated. The SQL is standard and runs on SQLite, which this schema resembles.

alternatives.interpretation: Ignore tracks with NULL Bytes entirely, so they contribute to neither the byte total, the millisecond total, nor the unit-price average for their media type.
alternatives.sql: WITH base AS (SELECT * FROM Track WHERE Bytes IS NOT NULL), per_media AS (SELECT MediaTypeId, AVG(UnitPrice) AS avg_price, 1.0 * SUM(Bytes) / SUM(Milliseconds) AS byte_rate FROM base GROUP BY MediaTypeId), overall AS (SELECT AVG(byte_rate) AS avg_rate FROM per_media), above AS (SELECT p.avg_price, p.byte_rate, p.byte_rate - o.avg_rate AS excess FROM per_media p CROSS JOIN overall o WHERE p.byte_rate > o.avg_rate) SELECT AVG(avg_price) AS avg_of_avg_unit_price, AVG(byte_rate) AS avg_byte_rate, AVG(excess) AS avg_excess_over_overall FROM above;
